description: SCIM runtime implementation is available only in EE builds.
SCIM administration and runtime require Pro tier or higher.
CE exposes no functioning SCIM service provider.
A sub-Pro tenant sees an upgrade state instead of SCIM setup controls.
Loss of Pro entitlement rejects new SCIM operations without changing existing state.
Restoring Pro entitlement resumes the preserved SCIM configuration.
Each tenant can configure at most one SCIM connection in the first release.
SCIM administration requires the existing security-settings permission.
An administrator can enable SCIM and receive a tenant-specific opaque base URL.
An administrator can generate a high-entropy SCIM bearer token shown once.
Alga persists only a secure hash of each SCIM bearer token.
SCIM token verification is timing-safe.
An administrator can rotate a SCIM token with a bounded overlap window.
An administrator can revoke either current or overlapping SCIM credentials immediately.
Disabling SCIM stops requests without changing links or user states.
SCIM authentication failures do not reveal another tenant, connection, token, or user.
SCIM requests are rate-limited per connection and source.
ServiceProviderConfig accurately describes supported and unsupported capabilities.
Schemas returns the supported SCIM user schema metadata.
ResourceTypes returns the supported Users resource and no Groups resource.
Users collection responses use SCIM media types and pagination metadata.
Users supports lookup by exact userName filter.
Users supports lookup by exact externalId filter.
Users/{id} returns a stable linked SCIM resource.
POST Users provisions a link without creating an Alga user.
PUT Users updates observed metadata and lifecycle state idempotently.
PATCH Users supports Entra-compatible active and observed-attribute operations.
DELETE Users performs reversible deprovisioning instead of hard deletion.
Unsupported filters return a standard invalidFilter SCIM error.
Malformed requests return sanitized standard SCIM error documents.
Unknown SCIM resource IDs return a tenant-safe not-found response.
SCIM Groups, Bulk, passwords, sorting, roles, and teams are unsupported.
Automatic linking considers existing internal MSP users only.
Automatic linking requires exactly one active unlinked user with an exact normalized primary-email match.
Automatic linking does not use aliases, UPN fallback, display names, fuzzy matching, or domain inference.
No exact match rejects provisioning without creating or modifying an Alga user.
Multiple exact matches reject provisioning without creating a link.
Unsupported or already-linked users reject provisioning without identity reassignment.
Rejected identities are upserted into a bounded unresolved-identity queue.
An administrator can explicitly link an unresolved identity to an eligible internal user.
Manual linking with mismatched email requires an explicit warning and confirmation.
A stable SCIM resource ID and upstream externalId correlate all operations after linking.
Database constraints prevent duplicate external identity links.
Database constraints prevent multiple active SCIM links for one internal user.
Observed email and profile attributes are stored on the link for drift reporting.
SCIM never automatically changes Alga email, username, name, title, or notifications.
SCIM never changes licenses, roles, teams, permissions, or authentication methods.
active=false marks the linked internal user inactive with SCIM provenance.
active=false revokes every active Alga session for the linked user.
The next authenticated request from a revoked prior session is denied across application pods.
DELETE preserves the Alga user, roles, assignments, and historical PSA records.
DELETE retains the identity link in a deprovisioned state.
active=true reactivates a user only when SCIM applied the current inactivity.
active=true never overrides manual or other-policy inactivity.
Repeated lifecycle requests are idempotent.
Concurrent lifecycle requests cannot reassign identities or overwrite newer authoritative state.
Manual activation is blocked while upstream SCIM state is inactive.
Explicit unlinking removes SCIM authority without changing effective user state.
Security settings includes a User provisioning surface adjacent to SSO.
The setup surface provides Entra-specific URL, token, mapping, assignment, and limitation guidance.
The setup surface shows enabled state, last request, last success, last sanitized error, and token age.
The setup surface provides token rotation and revocation controls with confirmations.
A linked-users view shows directory identity, Alga identity, upstream state, effective state, source, drift, and last operation.
An unresolved-identities view supports review and explicit resolution.
User Management marks linked internal users as Managed by SCIM.
User Management explains why upstream-inactive users cannot be activated locally.
SCIM disablement warns that current links and user states will be preserved.
Unlink confirmation warns that effective user state will not change.
Sanitized operation history records provisioning outcomes without raw payloads or secrets.
Security-sensitive setup, token, link, unlink, and lifecycle actions enter the Alga audit trail.
A Docker-capable TypeScript SCIM provisioning-client emulator runs locally and in CI.
The emulator supports deterministic users, assignment, enable, disable, delete, unassign, and reassign flows.
The emulator supports email/profile drift and stable external identity.
The emulator supports token rotation and records redacted request/response history.
The emulator supports duplicate delivery, concurrency, and stale-operation replay.
The emulator injects authentication, schema, filter, PATCH, timeout, and interrupted-response failures.
Emulator code and dependencies are excluded from production EE bundles.
A live Entra test enterprise application passes the supported provisioning lifecycle.
Customer documentation covers setup, mappings, lifecycle semantics, rotation, troubleshooting, and recovery.
